predecessors.name: Kingdom of Hungary
predecessors.text: the central Hungary that Cliopatria draws in its Kingdom of Hungary shape of 1540-1546: Buda and Pest, taken by trick on 29 August 1541

successors.name: Habsburg monarchy
successors.text: most of Hungary, ceded at Karlowitz; the Habsburgs administered an enlarged Kingdom of Hungary after 1699

ledger.x: 1541: the Ottomans take Buda and form Budin Eyalet.
1543-44: the Ottomans take more fortresses.
1552: northern expansion.
1552: the Eyalet of Temeşvar is established ('the new Eyalet of Temeşvar was established'); the Ottoman Hungary page lists it among the six eyalets.
1593: the Long Turkish War opens on Hungarian soil.
1594: the Ottomans take the two Danube fortresses.
1595: 'Mansfeld's Christian forces captured Esztergom and Visegrád on the Danube'.
1596: the Ottomans take Eger and form the Eğri eyalet.
1598: 'Habsburg forces retook Győr and Komárom'.
1600: the Kanije (Nagykanizsa) eyalet is established ('Kanije (1600)').
11 November 1606: the Peace of Zsitvatorok.
11 November 1606: Zsitvatorok ends the Long Turkish War; 'The war was indecisive, with little territory changing hands'.
27 August 1660: Nagyvárad (Oradea) falls to the Ottomans: 'The fall of Nagyvárad to the expansionist Ottomans on 27 August 1660 marked the decline of the Principality'.
1663: the Austro-Turkish War ('12 April 1663 - 10 August 1664') reaches Slovakia: the Ottoman army 'in September conquered the town of' Érsekújvár (Nové Zámky).
September 1663: Nové Zámky falls to the Ottomans and becomes the Uyvar frontier eyalet.
10 August 1664: 'the Peace of Vasvár was signed'; the Habsburgs recognise Ottoman control of 'Transylvania, Nagyvárad, and Érsekújvár'.

1683: the Great Turkish War: the main Ottoman army 'laid siege to Vienna on 14 July 1683'; the first ground lost in Hungary is Esztergom, which surrendered 'after a short siege' following the victory at Párkány in October 1683.
October 1683: 'Victory at Párkány in October 1683 led to Esztergom surrendering after a short siege.'
19 August 1685: 'Érsekújvár (Nové Zámky) fell on 19 August'.
2 September 1686: Buda falls.
1687: bridging.
January 1699: the Treaty of Karlowitz ends the Great Turkish War.
January 1699: 'the Ottomans recognized the loss of the Ottoman Hungary by the Treaty of Karlowitz in 1699'; 'The Ottomans ceded most of Hungary, Transylvania and Slavonia'.

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of central Hungary
wars.outcome: The Ottomans form Budin Eyalet in 1541, add Nógrád, Vác, Fehérvár, Pécs and Siklós in 1543-44 and create the Temeşvar eyalet in 1552.

wars.name: Long Turkish War
wars.outcome: Indecisive: the Ottomans kept Eger and Kanizsa, the Habsburgs got Vác; peace of Zsitvatorok on 11 November 1606.

wars.name: Austro-Turkish War (1663-1664)
wars.outcome: The Ottomans took Nové Zámky in September 1663 and kept it, with Nagyvárad, at the Peace of Vasvár on 10 August 1664.

wars.name: Great Turkish War
wars.outcome: The Holy League takes Esztergom (1683), Nové Zámky (1685), Buda (2 September 1686) and wins at Mohács (1687), Slankamen (1691) and Zenta (11 September 1697); Karlowitz in January 1699 cedes most of Hungary.

certainty.note: The frontier was a line of fortresses ('heavily fortified with troop garrisons'), not a survey line; the treaties of 1606 and 1664 name fortresses, not boundaries.
